exposure: Use of VITOM high-definition optical recording system during elective cesarean deliveries
outcome: Staff evaluations and remarks on image quality and delineation of anatomic landmarks
Trainee (medical students and residents) opinions on usefulness of VITOM experience
Scrubbed surgical technician and circulating nurse understanding of surgical layers and anticipation of steps
Ability of unscrubbed personnel and anesthesiologists to follow operation progression and blood loss
Use of recorded videos and still photographs in clinical teaching conferences and peer-reviewed publications
Setup time for the VITOM system
cohort: 104 patients undergoing elective cesarean deliveries (maternal ages 21-49 years) and 514 staff participants (trainee residents, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, medical students, surgical technicians, circulating nurses) in 3 designated operating rooms.
finding: The VITOM exoscope provided superb image quality, enabling clear vision of anatomic structures, reduced setup time, and received positive evaluations from staff and trainees, improving understanding of surgical steps and operating room efficiency, while also proving valuable for teaching and research.
